items.title: Dave Rivello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: And then, because of Gil Evans’ influence probably, I wanted to have a tuba.

ctx.x: Soprano, and he doubles on flute. And then tenor sax of course, and he doubles on flute and clarinet. And I like baritone saxophone but I really like bass clarinet. So there’s no baritone saxophone in my band, it’s bass clarinet and he doubles on flute and clarinet. And then, because of Gil Evans’ influence probably, I wanted to have a tuba. So two

trombones and a tuba. And then I thought about having French horn, also from Gil’s influence, but I thought if I’ve got one non-jazz guy, a tuba player, and I’m in Rochester, New York, two is probably going to be too much of a gamble. So I decided I have two trumpet players and I have the third guy only plays flugelhorn. So I think of that as kind of a French horn that blows forward instead of backwards. And that was I don’t have to deal with the acoustical issues of that also. And then piano, bass and drums, the…
